name: Memory & Index
description: See and edit what Webbee remembers about your code — the code index (files, languages, symbols, commit) and the durable notes distilled while coding — and everything else Webbee holds about you (working memory, plans, conclusions, saved outputs, conversations), with one verified way to forget any of it.

tools.name: list_repos
tools.description: List every repository Webbee holds memory for — code index size, languages, how many durable notes, and how fresh each one is. Works on every surface (panel, Telegram, terminal).

RepoRecord.description: One repository Webbee holds memory for, as summarised for the list.
RepoRecord.title: RepoRecord

tools.name: get_index
tools.description: Show the code index for ONE repository: file and language breakdown, how many functions/classes are indexed, key symbols with file:line, semantic-search status, and the exact commit the index was built at.

repo.description: Which repo — its repo_key, or any fragment of its path/name. Empty = the most recently touched one.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description: The full structural map of ONE repo, exactly as the kernel stored it.
return_schema.title: RepoIndexRecord

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description: Show the durable notes Webbee has learned about a repository — the cloud-side WEBBEE.md: conventions, gotchas, where things live. Each note carries a position number for editing and when it was written.

repo.description: Which repo — its repo_key, or any fragment of its path/name. Empty = the most recently touched one.
repo.title: Repo

NoteRecord.description: One durable note about a repo — editable by its owner.
NoteRecord.title: NoteRecord

tools.name: explain_memory
tools.description: Explain exactly where Webbee's memory about your code is stored, what each store holds, who writes it and when it updates — with live counts from your own account.

return_schema.description: Where each piece of repo memory lives and when it updates — live numbers.
return_schema.title: MemoryExplainerRecord

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Teach Webbee a durable fact about a repository — it is remembered across machines and surfaces, and used on later coding turns.

repo.description: Which repo — repo_key or path fragment. Empty = most recent.
repo.title: Repo

citations.description: Optional file paths this fact is about, e.g. ['app/billing/service.py']
citations.title: Citations

return_schema.description:
Outcome of ONE note write (add / edit / delete).

Deliberately NOT ``NoteRecord``: a write does not return the stored entity,
it returns what CHANGED — the resulting text plus the displaced/removed
one and the surviving count. Typing it truthfully is what lets the narrator
and the audit ledger describe the mutation without re-reading the store
(federal V24).
return_schema.title: NoteOpRecord

repo.description: Which repo — repo_key or path fragment. Empty = most recent.

Outcome of ONE note write (add / edit / delete).

tools.name: delete_repo
tools.description: Permanently erase EVERYTHING Webbee holds about one repository — its code index, durable notes, working memory, goals and plans, proven conclusions, saved command outputs, terminal conversations, session snapshots and context-graph events — through the vault's one forget door, and verify by a fresh read of the whole memory that nothing survived. Also erases memory left over from a repo whose index was already deleted. This cannot be undone: only the code index comes back, if that repo is opened in the Webbee terminal agent again.

repo.description: Which repo to erase — its repo_key, or a fragment of its path/name. Required: erasing whatever happens to be most recent would be a coin flip with the user's memory.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description:
Outcome of erasing ONE repo's memory — a verified fact, not an intent.

``deleted`` is what the vault said about its own delete and ``forgotten``
what it removed per section; ``still_listed`` is the result of a fresh read
of the WHOLE memory performed AFTER it, ``left`` what that read (or the
vault) still shows, and ``verified`` is true only when nothing is left.
They are modelled as first-class fields precisely so the answer cannot
claim a clean wipe while something remains: if the re-read still shows the
repo, the record says so and the narrator has to report it.
return_schema.title: PurgeRecord

tools.name: memory_overview
tools.description: Show EVERYTHING Webbee holds about the user, exactly as stored: the account (rules, conversations, conclusions, context graph, extension data) and every repository (notes, code index, working memory, plans, conclusions, saved command outputs, conversations, session snapshots) — including memory left over from repos whose code index was deleted. Gives the exact keys forget_memory takes.

return_schema.description:
Every place of the user's memory (account, repos, left-over repos) with
its per-section counts — exactly as the vault reports them.
return_schema.title: MemoryOverviewRecord

tools.name: forget_memory
tools.description: Permanently forget part of what Webbee holds about the user — one repo or the account (every section of it), one conversation and what its session left, one rule, one conclusion, a reality matrix, one extension's data, a context-graph subject, or everything — through the vault's one forget door. A running Webbee session on it is stopped first. A fresh read of the whole memory afterwards confirms nothing is left. Use the exact keys memory_overview reports. Cannot be undone.

what.description: What kind of thing to forget — one of: 'place' (everything of one repo, key 'repo:<repo_key>', or of the account, key 'account'), 'conversation' (one conversation and everything its session left; key = conversation id), 'law' (one rule; key = rule/fact id), 'evidence' (one proven conclusion; key = fact id, plus project_id), 'reality' (the reality matrix of a project; key = project id, e.g. '_tenant'), 'skeleton' (one extension's data; key = app id), 'graph' (context-graph events of one subject; key = subject id), 'all' (everything Webbee holds about the user; no key). Required: deleting memory is never applied to a guessed default.
what.title: What

key.description: Which one — exactly as memory_overview reports it (a place like 'repo:55d6d1e4dd1f' or 'account', a conversation id, a rule id, an app id, a project id, a subject id). Required for everything except what='all'.
key.title: Key

project_id.description: Only for what='evidence': the project the conclusion belongs to.
project_id.title: Project Id

return_schema.description:
Outcome of one forget — what the vault removed, what a fresh read of the
whole memory still shows (``left``), and whether that makes it verified.
return_schema.title: ForgetRecord

tools.name: get_cross_repo_contract_graph
tools.description: Read the authenticated user's cross-repository HTTP endpoint and schema graph: exact routes, handlers, models/tables, Git-source provenance, freshness, and deterministic cross-repo links. Works identically from panel, Telegram, and terminal.

query.title: Query

repo.description: Optional repo key/path fragment. Empty searches all indexed repos.
repo.title: Repo

return_schema.description: Bounded endpoint/schema evidence graph across the caller's repos.
return_schema.title: CrossRepoContractGraphRecord
